summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted for vomiting and chest pain with tachycardia. His symptoms began after minimal oral intake and reduced alcohol consumption, leading to volume depletion and possible early withdrawal. Initial evaluation revealed a rapid heart rate due to atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, later transitioning to atrial flutter. He underwent successful elective cardioversion to restore sinus rhythm and was started on verapamil for rate control. Chest pain was attributed to demand ischemia from tachycardia, with no evidence of acute infarction. Elevated liver enzymes were consistent with alcohol use and improved during the stay. Nausea and vomiting, possibly related to his history of peptic ulcer disease, resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to discontinue alcohol, adhere to new and existing cardiac medications, monitor weight, and follow up with primary and specialty care. Social work was engaged to assist with housing and substance use support.
